messages:
maya: Quick update — ran the full eval for orion14b-int6 -> int8 quant path. Unit econ: int8 is ~2.1x cheaper per token vs int6 baseline (batching similar). We do see regressions on a couple of slices: longform summaries and safety-sensitive QA.

devin: Numbers? what's the delta on summary / QA?

maya: Short version: Rouge-L median drop ~0.7 pts, 95th percentile drop ~2.8 pts for >512-token summaries. Answer-exactness (closed-book QA) overall -0.4% but -1.9% on the "financial_doc" slice.

alex: Cost side: int8 p50 latency +4ms, p95 +12ms in our infra tests, but cost per 1M tokens down from $320 -> $150 (rough numbers).

sam_product: @maya are those regressions acceptable for GTN? Product wants overall <1% QA regressions and minimal summary quality loss.

maya: Not acceptable straight up. Proposal: hybrid routing — default to int8, route requests that match safety or longform detectors to int6. Offline sim shows this keeps global QA regression <0.6% while preserving ~1.8-1.9x cost reduction.

devin: How would we detect those slices in real time? Cheap signal or heavyweight classifier?

alex: We prototyped a light probe classifier (5-layer MLP over token-embeddings + length/domain tag). Inference cost ~1.2ms p50, FP rate ~6%, TP ~87% on validation slice.

maya: Threshold tuning: classifier_confidence > 0.7 => route to int6. Offline sim (traffic replay) metrics: cost saving 1.9x, global QA regression 0.35%, fallback rate ~12.3% on our sample traffic.

sam_product: Good. We need a compact scorecard for GTN: unit economics (savings), SLO risk, fallback rates, and example failing prompts. Can you draft a 1‑pager? :thumbsup:

maya: Will do. Draft routing rule below (prototype):

```yaml
routing:
  default_model: orion14b-int8
  signals:
    - name: early_risk_classifier
      type: float_confidence
      threshold: 0.7
      action: route_to
      target: orion14b-int6
  canary: {percent: 1, duration_hours: 48}
  rollback_policy:
    - metric: QA_degradation_pct
      threshold: 0.5
      window_minutes: 60
      action: rollback
```

alex: Offline observed metrics (sample):
- baseline_cost_per_M: $320
- int8_cost_per_M: $150
- simulated_cost_saving: 1.9x
- classifier_fallback_rate: 12.3%
- QA_regression_global: 0.35%
- QA_regression_financial_slice: 0.6%
- summary_tail_degradation_95pct: 1.9 pts

devin: Edge case: very long sequences (>=2048) and mid-request fallback — do we pre-warm kv-cache or do a strict routing at request-accept time? Mid-request switch is messy.

maya: Plan: decision at accept-time only. If classifier marks risky, route to int6 from the start. For requests where risk appears mid-stream we currently mark result as degraded and prefer to return partial + user hint. Also proposing to disable mid-request fallback to avoid cross-device state churn.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduler: canary scheduled 2026-04-02T14:00:00Z (1% traffic, 48h). Auto-rollback rule requires QA_degradation > 0.5% sustained for 1h to trigger.

sam_product: OK — thanks. Maya, please post the 1-pager + sample failing prompts before tomorrow sync (10:00am PT). We'll use that in the GTN brief.

maya: On it. Will include example prompts, traffic sims, and the A/B artifact for validation.
